findings.description: The version-pin assertion accesses `jsonschema.__version__` directly, which emits a DeprecationWarning in jsonschema>=4.x: 'Accessing jsonschema.__version__ is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Use importlib.metadata directly to query for jsonschema's version.' This warning is visible in the CI run log (run 25234128260). The assertion succeeds and the warning does not break the step; it produces noise in the runner log.
findings.recommendation: Replace `jsonschema.__version__` with `importlib.metadata.version('jsonschema')` in the assertion string when the equivalent change is made in policy-check.yml (symmetric treatment). Forward-compat: file as TF or address in a future lockfile-bump PR. Not a blocker for this slice.
findings.rationale: The same pattern exists in policy-check.yml (four sites), so this is consistent pre-existing behaviour that has been accepted across both workflows. Fixing it here alone would introduce asymmetry; symmetric remediation is the right path. Non-blocking.

findings.description: `bash -n .github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml` exits 2 with 'syntax error near unexpected token ('' at line 37 ('- name: Install Python dependencies (hash-pinned)'). This is a known bash-parser false positive: `bash -n` treats YAML files as shell scripts and chokes on parentheses in YAML step-name strings. The file is not executed by bash directly — GitHub Actions parses it as YAML and passes the `run:` block content to bash. CI confirms clean execution (run 25234128260, step completes successfully). The DISPATCH-NOTE item (viii) specifies `bash -n` as acceptance criterion, but this false positive is structural and unresolvable without renaming the step.
findings.recommendation: Accept the false positive and document it in the DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion (viii) as 'bash -n reports a false positive on YAML step names containing parentheses; CI execution confirms the run: block is syntactically valid bash'. Alternatively rename the step to remove the parentheses, e.g. 'Install Python dependencies — hash-pinned'.
findings.rationale: bash -n on a YAML file is an imperfect lint proxy; the actual execution path (GitHub Actions parsing YAML then running the run: block through bash -e) is what matters. CI green confirms correctness. The naming convention with parentheses is consistent with the pre-existing 'Install pinned OPA runtime' step style.
